subtitleTiming: Script-timed draft; align to the final voiceover before submission.

chapters.title: A night changes
chapters.reference: Anthony Mitchell and the Eaton Fire

chapters.title: Maya asks for help
chapters.reference: A warning call from Standard Response

shots.title: Maya with friends. Warm light. Happy music.
shots.instruction: Film Maya laughing with friends indoors. Establish her face and a distinctive jacket. Warm light; 2–3 short shots within this single 9-second clip. Original upbeat music is included.
shots.caption: [Upbeat music]

shots.title: The same Maya. Outside. Alone in the dark.
shots.instruction: Hard cut to the SAME actor in the SAME jacket outside. Cool light, quiet surroundings, glance at phone. Use a controlled filming location. No repeated party footage.
shots.caption: [Music stops. Quiet night ambience.]

shots.title: Safety concerns are real
shots.instruction: Included animated statistic. Source and population stay visible.
shots.voice: In a 2019 survey across thirty-three universities, thirteen percent of student respondents reported nonconsensual sexual contact involving force or inability to consent since enrolling.
shots.detail: Student respondents reported nonconsensual sexual contact involving force or inability to consent since enrollment.

shots.title: The context of a night out
shots.instruction: Included statistic. Separate population and timeframe; do not imply drinking causes victimization.
shots.voice: In a separate 2024 survey, one in four full-time college students aged eighteen to twenty-five reported binge drinking in the past month.
shots.detail: Full-time U.S. college students, ages 18–25, reported binge drinking in the past month.

shots.title: A request needs a response.
shots.instruction: Included animated design rationale. This is the product goal, not an effectiveness claim.
shots.voice: These figures describe different risks, not a causal link. SafeNight is designed to turn a request for help into an acknowledged response.

shots.title: Back to Maya: “I feel unsafe”
shots.instruction: Same actor and exterior. Over-shoulder shot opening SafeNight and tapping the unsafe/help action. If exact wording is unavailable, use a labeled prototype; never pass it off as the implemented UI.
shots.voice: Back outside, Maya opens SafeNight and taps, I feel unsafe.

shots.title: Maya gets an incoming SafeNight call
shots.instruction: Film the same actor answering a staged call. Use only test devices. Proposed voice integration; label simulation.
shots.voice: In this proposed flow, SafeNight calls her.

shots.title: SafeNight confirms the shared details
shots.instruction: Film Maya listening on the phone. Record the AI lines in the chapter audio. Use fictional name and location, with the actor’s response next.
shots.voice: Maya, this is SafeNight responding to your request. You shared the east entrance. Is that correct, and are you safe?
shots.speaker: SafeNight

shots.title: Maya confirms: “I don’t feel safe”
shots.instruction: Same actor answers naturally. This explicitly authorizes the staged campus-safety request; no real service is contacted.
shots.voice: That’s right. I don’t feel safe. Please contact campus safety.
shots.speaker: Maya

shots.title: SafeNight explains the next step
shots.instruction: Hold on the same actor listening. Do not imply help has arrived or an institution has accepted the request.
shots.voice: I’ll send your confirmed location and request. I’m waiting for their acknowledgment.
shots.speaker: SafeNight

shots.title: Message to a simulated campus-safety desk
shots.instruction: Add a staged test-receiver capture: Maya requested help; east entrance confirmed; timestamp; callback; acknowledgment pending. Mark SIMULATED throughout. No live police, dispatch, or campus-safety messages.
shots.voice: The proposed handoff sends the confirmed details to an authorized campus-safety channel. This demonstration uses a simulated receiver.

shots.title: Now dive into the actual app
shots.instruction: Record the actual Night Out group, membership, and approved buddies. Maya is the protagonist throughout. Preserve mock-data labels.
shots.voice: Now let’s look inside SafeNight. A Night Out connects the group. Each person chooses their sharing permissions and approved contacts before the night begins.

shots.title: Follow the actual incident timeline
shots.instruction: Record the real incident panel with plan versions and tool receipts. Keep simulated labels. Do not imply the staged phone call is implemented.
shots.voice: The incident timeline brings requests, responses, plans, and tool receipts together. Simulated actions stay labeled, so the demo separates the working interface from proposed integrations.

shots.title: Show an approved friend accepting
shots.instruction: Record the actual approved-buddy acknowledgment, with the same Maya incident if supported. If unavailable, leave this card until recorded.
shots.voice: An approved friend can acknowledge the request. The group can see the difference between a message being sent and someone agreeing to help.

shots.title: Show sharing permissions
shots.instruction: Record actual per-person consent controls and update timestamps. Do not revoke consent during an active recording unless demonstrating that behavior.
shots.voice: Location sharing stays scoped and visible. The response uses information the person chose to share, and keeps stale updates distinct from confirmed details.

shots.title: Show the plan and follow-up
shots.instruction: Record actual permitted tool receipts and follow-up state. Label the simulated planner unless live Nemotron is verified.
shots.voice: Nemotron is intended to interpret context and coordinate permitted tools. SpacetimeDB owns the durable state, permissions, and follow-up logic. Immediate alerts stay independent of AI.

shots.title: Acknowledge the handoff
shots.instruction: Record the actual approved-buddy response or a clearly simulated institutional acknowledgment. Do not equate message delivery with responder acceptance.
shots.voice: A sent message is not a completed handoff. The workflow tracks acknowledgment and keeps unresolved needs visible until a person confirms who is taking responsibility.

shots.title: Return to Maya: an explicit check-in
shots.instruction: Film the same actor with an approved friend, then the actual human-confirmation action. Use the UI’s real wording; preserve prototype labels if needed.
shots.voice: When Maya can confirm her status, she checks in explicitly. The incident closes through human confirmation, rather than assuming a location update means everything is okay.

shots.title: Show the completed timeline
shots.instruction: Record the actual timeline. Avoid invented response-time or safety-improvement numbers.
shots.voice: One timeline: the request, the response, the handoff, and the confirmed outcome.

shots.title: Go out together. Get home together.
shots.instruction: Included closing card.
shots.voice: SafeNight. Go out together. Get home together.
